column3: The Hebrew says that one tribe will be “for him”; BSB says it will remain, leaving the beneficiary implicit.
The Hebrew says “his father David”; BSB identifies the possessive as Solomon’s.
The Hebrew leaves Solomon unnamed and says “I will make him a ruler”; BSB names Solomon and says “I have made him ruler.”
The Hebrew first names taking the kingdom and then identifies the gift as the ten tribes; BSB combines this as taking ten tribes of the kingdom.
The Hebrew says “your soul desires”; BSB says “your heart desires.”
The Hebrew promises “a faithful house”; BSB renders this as “a lasting dynasty.”
The Hebrew uses collective singular “seed”; BSB says “descendants.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Egypt as where he remained; BSB uses “where.”
The Hebrew calls the period “the days”; BSB uses “the time.”
